purpose: Generate manuscript-facing data tables without recomputing or reselecting scientific endpoints.

figure1.title: Study system and ecological state hierarchy

panels.A: 71 stable Tampa transects with water-body identity and coordinates
panels.B: Stable-node versus year descriptive R2 for recorded detection, frequency, Braun-Blanquet, blade length and shoot density

figure1.claim: Occurrence/abundance levels are much more site-anchored than plant-condition traits.

figure2.title: Persistent occurrence with bay-specific quantitative degradation

panels.A_D: 2016-2025 segment-year trajectories for detection plus relevant quantitative state dimensions
panels.E: Canonical within-transect slope summary and bootstrap intervals

figure2.claim: Old, Middle and Lower Tampa Bay show distinct degradation modes beneath weak binary change.

figure3_tampa.title: Community reorganization in Lower Tampa Bay

panels.A: 2016-2025 Thalassia, Syringodium and Halodule frequency trajectories

figure3_tampa.claim: Lower Tampa Bay shows compositional reorganization, not proof of competitive replacement.

figure3_nps.title: External Zostera state decoupling
figure3_nps.claim: Saturated recorded presence can coexist with large quantitative cover trajectories in a second monitoring system.

figure4.title: Quantitative state before next-year recorded loss

panels.A: Source-year focal frequency before persistence versus loss
panels.B: Source-year Braun-Blanquet state before persistence versus loss

figure4.claim: Quantitative degradation is an internal exploratory early-warning candidate for recorded-state instability.

rules: Do not omit adverse target year 2016 from Figure 4 primary panel.
Do not plot Braun-Blanquet as percent cover; label as ordinal abundance index.
Do not show mechanism-null screens as a main figure unless manuscript structure changes prospectively.
Do not use Figure 1 stable-node R2 as a causal variance partition.
Do not infer competitive replacement from Figure 3 Tampa community trajectories.
